effectiveDate.original: 19/30 сентября 1721 г. — размен ратификационных грамот в Ништадте

geometry.derivationNote: The Treaty of Nystad and verified exchange of ratifications establish the exact legal transition. The pinned 1721–1726 Cliopatria/Seshat state is independently spatially controlled and corroborated by those treaty sources; for replay the Nystad transition replaces the pre-treaty full state with that verified post-ratification full state rather than approximating the acquisition as a modern regional polygon.

territoryChanges.notes: Geometry-verified as a full-state replacement on the verified ratification-exchange date; detailed surveyed line precision remains medium-confidence.

effectiveDate.original: 2 (14) июля 1812 г. — размен ратификационных грамот в Бухаресте

geometry.derivationNote: Article 4 gives a direct legal route: the Prut from its entry into Moldavia to its confluence with the Danube, with the middle of the Prut as the interstate boundary; from that confluence the left bank of the Danube continues to the Kilia mouth and the sea, subject to the treaty's explicit special treatment of small islands and the two large islands opposite Ismail and Kilia. Territory on the left bank of the Prut is ceded to Russia. Article 6 restores the Asian frontier to its pre-war position rather than creating a new exact Asian line. Historical river-channel geometry and island positions still require period hydrography; the treaty text must not be snapped to modern channels without evidence.

territoryChanges.notes: The treaty states that the peace act is completed by mutual exchange of ratifications; the verified exchange date is therefore used for territorial replay rather than the 28 May signature date.

effectiveDate.original: 30 декабря 1920 г. — вторая подпись; договор вступает в силу с момента подписания

geometry.derivationNote: The treaty defines a mixed route: along the Selenga to Lake Baikal; through Lake Baikal using the former Irkutsk/Transbaikal administrative division; onward by former Yakut and Far-Eastern regional boundaries, then watershed systems to the Sea of Okhotsk near Cape Madzhalida. It also allocates the islands south of the specified parallel, including northern Sakhalin, to the Far Eastern Republic and requires a mixed commission to mark the line. On rivers and lakes the treaty uses the middle of the navigable part. Exact geometry therefore depends on period administrative-boundary maps, hydrography and commission marking evidence; no modern oblast/republic boundary may be substituted automatically.

territoryChanges.notes: The RSFSR counterpart is dated 15 December and the FER counterpart 30 December 1920. Because the treaty says it enters into force from the moment of signing, 30 December is used conservatively as the first date on which both counterpart signatures existed.
